title: One who is skilled in the goal, One who knows the peaceful path, Should act like this: After understanding clearly, Being capable, upright, Truly, well…
content:
One who is skilled in the goal,
One who knows the peaceful path,
Should act like this:
After understanding clearly,
Being capable, upright,
Truly, well direct, easy to speak to,
Gentle, without conceit.

Content, easily supported,
With few duties, living simply,
With peaceful faculties, wise,
Not arrogant, without greed for families.

One should not commit any trivial fault
That other wise people might criticize.
May all beings be happy and secure,
May they attain happiness and well-being.

Whatever living beings there are,
Frail or strong, without exception,
Long or large, medium or short,
Subtle or gross, seen or unseen,
Those living far or near,
Those already born or seeking birth,
May all beings be happy and well.

title: Māluṅkyaputta, just as a man shot with a dart thickly smeared with poison. His friends and relatives summon a surgeon. But the man says: 'I…
content: Māluṅkyaputta, just as a man shot with a dart thickly smeared with poison. His friends and relatives summon a surgeon. But the man says: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know whether the man who shot me was a noble, a brahmin, a merchant, or a worker.' He might say: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know the name and clan of the man who shot me.' He might say: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know whether the man who shot me was tall, short, or of medium height.' He might say: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know whether the man who shot me was dark, tawny, or golden.' ... Māluṅkyaputta, that man would die and still not know these things. So too, Māluṅkyaputta, whoever says: 'I will not live the holy life under the Blessed One until he answers me: "The world is eternal" or "the world is not eternal" ... "the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death" — that person will die and still not have had these things answered by the Tathāgata. Māluṅkyaputta, the holy life does not depend on the view that the world is eternal. The holy life does not depend on the view that the world is not eternal. Whether there is the view that the world is eternal or the view that the world is not eternal, there is still birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, and I teach their abandonment here and now.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, a tree with its branches and leaves destroyed: then its shoots do not reach completeness, its bark does not reach completeness, its…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, a tree with its branches and leaves destroyed: then its shoots do not reach completeness, its bark does not reach completeness, its sapwood does not reach completeness, its heartwood does not reach completeness. So too, bhikkhus, for an immoral person, one of broken virtue, right concentration is thereby destroyed. When right concentration is absent, for one whose right concentration is destroyed, true knowledge and vision of things as they really are is thereby destroyed. When true knowledge and vision is absent, for one whose true knowledge and vision is destroyed, disenchantment and dispassion are thereby destroyed. When disenchantment and dispassion are absent, for one whose disenchantment and dispassion are destroyed, the knowledge and vision of liberation is thereby destroyed.

title: He drenches, saturates, fills, and suffuses his body with the rapture and ease born of concentration, so that no part of his entire body is…
content: He drenches, saturates, fills, and suffuses his body with the rapture and ease born of concentration, so that no part of his entire body is not suffused with that rapture and ease born of concentration. Great king, this is a visible fruit of the ascetic life, more excellent and sublime than previous visible fruits of the ascetic life.

title: Here, Udāyi, a person lives dedicated to the abandoning of bases, to the relinquishment of bases. But while he lives dedicated to the abandoning of…
content: Here, Udāyi, a person lives dedicated to the abandoning of bases, to the relinquishment of bases. But while he lives dedicated to the abandoning of bases, to the relinquishment of bases, thoughts and reflections connected with bases arise. He tolerates them, does not abandon them, does not relinquish them, does not terminate them, does not destroy them. Udāyi, I say: 'That person is bound, not unbound.' Why is that? Because the difference in his faculties is clearly known to me.

title: On the slopes of the Snowy Mountain lives a tribe of upright people, With abundant wealth and energy, in the Kosala land. Born in the…
content:
On the slopes of the Snowy Mountain lives a tribe of upright people,
With abundant wealth and energy, in the Kosala land.

Born in the solar clan, the Sakya family,
Leaving that family, I went forth, O king.
I have no longing for sensual pleasures.

Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures, abandoning them is security.
I will go, striving; my mind is joyful.

title: Easy to do is a good deed For one who does good; Hard to do is an evil deed For one who does good. Easy…
content:
Easy to do is a good deed
For one who does good;
Hard to do is an evil deed
For one who does good.

Easy to do is an evil deed
For one who does evil;
Hard to do is a good deed
For the noble ones.

title: Here, bhikkhus, a person, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna. Regarding whatever things there are there…
content: Here, bhikkhus, a person, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna. Regarding whatever things there are there — form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — he contemplates them as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, a boil, a dart, a misfortune, an affliction, as alien, as decaying, as empty, as not-self. After death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in companionship with the devas of the Pure Abodes. This kind of rebirth, bhikkhus, is not shared with ordinary persons.

title: Elder Nun Sumedhā: The daughter of King Koñca, With the chief queen, In Mātavatī, Sumedhā was born. Joyfully striving to practice The Teacher's instruction. Skilled…
content:
Elder Nun Sumedhā:

The daughter of King Koñca,
With the chief queen,
In Mātavatī,
Sumedhā was born.
Joyfully striving to practice
The Teacher's instruction.

Skilled in virtue, well taught,
Learned, well trained,
Following the Buddha's teaching,
She went to her parents and said:
'Please, mother and father,
Both of you, listen to me!

'I rejoice in Nibbāna,
Even the existence of devas
Is impermanent.
What value are sensual pleasures?
Empty, with little sweetness,
Their harm is great.

'Sensual pleasures are truly bitter,
Like the venom of a poisonous snake.
Only fools are infatuated
With such sensual pleasures.
Those who enjoy sensual pleasures
For a long time
Suffer the torments of hell,
Afflicted and harmed.

'Those who do evil deeds,
Those with evil minds,
Experience painful suffering
In the realm of misery.
Fools do not restrain
Body, speech, and mind.

'Fools of weak wisdom,
Do not think, do not decide,
Do not stop the origin of suffering
When the time for teaching comes,
Do not care to learn,
Do not realize the noble truths.

'These truths, dear mother,
The supreme Buddha taught.
Most beings
Do not understand those truths.
They delight in renewed existence,
Long to be born in heaven.

'Birth in heaven is not lasting,
Existence is impermanent.
Fools are not afraid,
They are always reborn.

'Falling into the four lower realms,
Being born in heaven or human realm —
Hard it is to be born there.
Those who fall into the lower realms,
Into the realm of hell,
Have no chance to go forth.

'Please, both mother and father,
Let me go forth
In the teaching proclaimed
By the One with Ten Powers,
Living at ease,
Striving to end birth and death.

'Why should I delight in renewed existence
With this sinful body,
Empty, without core?
For the purpose of destroying
The craving for renewed existence,
Please let me go forth.

'Now a Buddha has arisen,
The wrong time is abandoned.
The time has now come.
Throughout my life,
I will not injure the precepts and the holy life.'

title: Bhikkhus, here the third class of samaṇas and brahmins reflects: 'This first class... did not escape Māra's power. This second class... also did not escape…
content: Bhikkhus, here the third class of samaṇas and brahmins reflects: 'This first class... did not escape Māra's power. This second class... also did not escape Māra's power. Let us make a hiding place near the bait spread by Māra and the world's goods. Having made a hiding place there, without entering, without indulging, we will consume the bait and the world's goods. By not entering, not indulging, we will not become confused; not confused, we will not become heedless; not heedless, we will not be at the will of Māra among that bait and those world's goods.' They make a hiding place near the bait... without entering, without indulging, they consume the bait... not becoming confused... not heedless... not at the will of Māra. But then they hold such wrong views as: 'The world is eternal; the world is not eternal; the world is finite; the world is infinite; ...' Thus, bhikkhus, this third class of samaṇas and brahmins does not escape Māra's power.
